summary: Milestone 2026.05.120 completed the supplied operational slice in 40 minutes across 11 completed experiments, averaging 4 minutes per experiment. The slowest-five timing was almost entirely gate-bound: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 entries gated on the Exp 1414 repair-executor path consumed 25 minutes (62.5%), the recurring Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 gate consumed 10 minutes (25%), and a SOTA GGUF cache/provenance doomed-rerun preflight consumed 2 minutes (5%). Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout and during local verification, with only 4 MB allocated per GPU, 0% utilization, no GPU compute processes, and no gpu_monitor.py-class zombies. Estimated next-milestone savings are 55% if duplicate same-verdict gates terminalize, known readiness checks move to activation time, independent lanes run concurrently, and docs reconciliation becomes idempotent.
timing_data_caveat: The supplied slowest-experiment labels reference recurring gate classes and earlier experiment IDs. This artifact treats those labels as authoritative timing evidence for the 2026.05.120 operational slice, while using exp1560-exp1573 local artifacts only for milestone context.

research_milestone_context.context_summary: Milestone .120 covered THRML/block-Gibbs security and sampler discipline, BRAIN+Linear-AR rescue falsification, SpecAnn rejection, soft-Gibbs residuals, candidate warm-start benchmarking, rho(C) measurement, FR-11 retained-policy audit, soft-Gibbs coverage bounds, and AR-REINFORCE baseline checks. This operational retro evaluates execution efficiency rather than research merit.

slowest_experiments.why_slow: The full-pipeline path remained schedulable while gated on repair-executor availability, instead of requiring fresh nonzero accepted-repair evidence or a changed downstream contract before rerun.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] arXiv Bundle v10 - Gated on Exp 1269 Critical Fixes
slowest_experiments.why_slow: A known legacy publication gate continued to consume milestone wall time instead of terminalizing at activation with explicit unchanged upstream state.

slowest_experiments.why_slow: This was duplicate same-dependency pipeline churn. After the first unchanged gate verdict, reruns should have been suppressed until repair evidence or validator contracts changed.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Full-Scale Pipeline v3 - Gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor
slowest_experiments.why_slow: Another repeated pipeline attempt consumed time without evidence of new repair outputs, a new candidate pool, or a changed gate contract.

slowest_experiments.label: -0400 [conductor] Doomed-rerun block: SOTA GGUF Cache + Provenance Preflight - P
slowest_experiments.why_slow: A cache/provenance readiness failure was discovered as a scheduled runtime slot. It should be a fast structured activation preflight with explicit missing-cache and provenance fields.

bottlenecks_identified: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gate churn consumed 25 of 40 minutes (62.5%) across three slowest-five entries.
The Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 legacy gate consumed 10 minutes (25%) despite being a recurring known-blocked publication path.
The SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight still appeared as a doomed-rerun execution slot instead of an activation-time readiness artifact.
GPU utilization was inefficient for any LLM-bearing work: both RTX 3090s were idle with 4 MB allocated and 0% utilization.
No material GPU zombie processes were present; the resource issue was idle scheduler capacity, not leaked VRAM.

Several .120 lanes could have overlapped after activation: Kinetic Defense, BRAIN k-sweep, and SpecAnn ADR were independent; soft-Gibbs residuals, rho(C) measurement, and FR-11 retained-policy audit were also independent; downstream warm-start, coverage-bound, and AR-REINFORCE checks had narrow direct gates and did not need a globally sequential schedule.

The pre-flight suite was not the dominant wall-time bottleneck in the supplied slowest-five data, but broad full-suite execution remains a risk because exp1564 hit an unrelated full_tests_python hang.
Documentation reconciliation was not a top-five timing item, but closeout still depends on manual append-only updates to changelog and roadmap files.
The operational retro relied on manually supplied timing labels rather than a structured conductor timing ledger, limiting root-cause precision.
improvements_suggested: Require nonzero accepted-repair evidence, changed repair artifacts, or nonzero pipeline improvement before scheduling Full-Scale Pipeline reruns.
Add same-verdict retirement for repeated Full-Scale Pipeline gate attempts within a milestone.
Terminalize Exp 1269 arXiv Bundle v10 and SOTA GGUF cache/provenance readiness at activation time unless their upstream state changed.
Persist before/after gpu_monitor.py snapshots in every GPU-bearing result artifact, including process count, utilization, VRAM, and DualGPURunner lane assignment.
Use DualGPURunner by default for independent Qwen/Gemma local SOTA checks when both RTX 3090s are free.

Fan out independent .120-style lanes once direct gates pass: activation-gated security/ADR/sampler checks, soft-Gibbs/rho(C)/FR-11 audits, and benchmark follow-ups should run as separate dependency lanes.
Keep preflight checks cluster-scoped until broad full-suite/spec-coverage debt is green enough for blanket gating.
Make docs reconciliation a no-op-aware command keyed by milestone and experiment id so changelog and roadmap rows are appended exactly once.
Store a structured conductor timing ledger with categories for gate wait, preflight, GPU inference, CPU analysis, docs reconciliation, and artifact write time.
Require future operational-retro prompts to carry milestone-local timing snapshots so retros do not need to infer current efficiency from recurring older gate labels.
savings_basis: The supplied slowest five account for 37 of 40 minutes. Not all 37 minutes can be removed because terminal gate artifacts and small diagnostics still have real cost, but eliminating duplicate pipeline churn, terminalizing legacy arXiv/cache checks, and overlapping independent work should plausibly recover about 22 minutes.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Terminalize repeated Full-Scale Pipeline same-verdict gates
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: Three Full-Scale Pipeline v3 entries dominated the timing. Reruns should require changed repair evidence or nonzero downstream improvement.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Move arXiv and SOTA GGUF readiness checks to activation-time terminal artifacts
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: The 10 minute arXiv gate and 2 minute cache/provenance block are known readiness states that should not consume scheduled runtime slots.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions.action: Enforce dependency-lane fanout plus DualGPURunner telemetry
top_3_highest_leverage_actions.rationale: Several .120 checks were independent after activation, and both GPUs were idle. Explicit lane assignment would expose missed parallelism and prevent silent sequential fallback.

questions_answered.which_experiments_took_the_longest_and_w: Full-Scale Pipeline v3 gated on Exp 1414 Repair Executor was the dominant path: 14, 6, and 5 minute entries totaling 25 minutes because the gate allowed repeated pipeline validation without new nonzero repair evidence. arXiv Bundle v10 gated on Exp 1269 consumed another 10 minutes as a recurring legacy publication gate. The SOTA GGUF cache/provenance preflight consumed 2 minutes rediscovering a known readiness failure.
questions_answered.was_gpu_utilization_efficient_sequential: No. The supplied and verified gpu_monitor.py snapshots show both RTX 3090s at 4/24576 MB and 0% utilization with no compute processes. Any live Qwen/Gemma model lanes should have used DualGPURunner across GPU 0 and GPU 1, while CPU-only analysis and docs tasks ran independently.
questions_answered.were_there_zombie_processes_wasting_reso: No. gpu_monitor.py reported an empty process list and no warnings. The residual 4 MB allocation per GPU is below the script's 1024 MB zombie threshold and is consistent with driver/context residue, not material VRAM waste.
questions_answered.could_any_experiments_have_been_parallel: Yes. Kinetic Defense, BRAIN+Linear-AR k-sweep, and SpecAnn ADR were all activation-gated and independent. Soft-Gibbs residual work, rho(C) measurement, and FR-11 retained-policy auditing could also run in parallel. Candidate warm-start benchmarking, soft-Gibbs coverage validation, and AR-REINFORCE checks had narrow direct gates and should not force a globally sequential milestone.
questions_answered.was_the_preflight_test_suite_a_bottlenec: Not the dominant bottleneck in the supplied timing. Only 2 minutes of the slowest five are directly preflight-like, versus 25 minutes for pipeline gate churn and 10 minutes for the arXiv gate. However, exp1564 still hit an unrelated full_tests_python hang, so preflight and verification should remain cluster-scoped until broad-suite debt is resolved.
questions_answered.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: They were not measured as a slowest-five bottleneck, but they remain structurally inefficient because closeout still depends on manual append-only updates. Idempotent docs appenders would reduce closeout friction and duplicate-row risk.
questions_answered.what_tooling_infrastructure_changes_woul: Nonzero-success gates, same-verdict retirement, activation-time readiness artifacts, DualGPURunner lane assignment, per-experiment GPU telemetry, cluster-scoped preflight, structured conductor timing categories, and idempotent changelog/roadmap appenders.

preflight_suite.assessment: The preflight suite was not the main timing bottleneck in this slice, but readiness checks should become fast terminal artifacts and broad-suite checks should remain scoped until unrelated hangs are retired.

doc_reconciliation.assessment: Manual docs reconciliation was short but structurally avoidable. The conductor should expose an idempotent docs closeout command that appends changelog and roadmap rows exactly once.

meta_reflection: The milestone is already short in absolute time, so the remaining gains come from scheduler discipline rather than faster individual agents. Available hardware is not the same as used hardware, and blocked readiness is not worth rediscovering during scheduled execution. The conductor should make unchanged gates terminal, make independent lanes explicit, and record timing in a structured ledger so the next retro can audit facts instead of reconstructing them.
